title: Fabrication and optimization of a multielectrode microfluidic electrochemical flow cell for fast and dynamic detection of reaction products
author: Fanavoll, Harrington, et al.
materials: In the final electrochemical setup, the primary inlet is connected to a syringe in a programmable syringe pump or pressure pump, while the reference channel inlet is connected to a free syringe. The side channel with the reference electrode was kept stagnant during measurements. The side channel was flushed regularly with supporting electrolyte from the connected syringe. PDMS is oxygen permeable, so it is necessary to keep the microfluidic cell under an inert atmosphere during experiments. A conventional airtight polypropylene/silicone box (∼10 × 15 cm2 and thickness ∼1 mm) was modified to keep the microfluidic electrochemical cell in an oxygen-free environment (see Fig. 8), while still providing electrolyte input and connection to a potentiostat. The cells were mounted and left in the box under inert gas for at least 4 hours, and sometimes overnight, before use to remove oxygen from the PDMS. Either argon or nitrogen gas purging was used, though in this case nitrogen gas may be more effective at purging the oxygen from the cell, as N2 is more permeable in PDMS than both O2 and Ar [7,8]. The microfluidic flow cells may also be stored in a glove box for a time before use.Fig. 8The electrochemical setup for microfluidic cells. The primary inlet is connected to a glass syringe in a syringe pump (left). The inlet tubing is kept inside the purged atmosphere using flexible tubes. Connecting leads to the potentiostats are entering through sealed holes in the box (bottom right). Spent electrolyte is collected in a glass beaker.Fig. 8

steps.title: Clean and Bond PDMS to Electrode Slide
steps.instruction: Thoroughly clean the finished PDMS slab with Scotch™ tape to remove PDMS residue and dust. Place both the electrode slide and the PDMS slab in a plasma cleaner for 24 s at 50 W with oxygen flow to activate surfaces. Within 1 min of plasma activation, align the channel over the electrodes and bring the two parts into contact to form a partial irreversible bond; avoid peeling or realignment as it can rip PDMS. Bake the assembled cell at 80 °C for at least 20 min to complete bonding. Note that the PDMS will not bond irreversibly to metal surfaces.

steps.title: Solder Electrical Connections to Contact Plates
steps.instruction: Cut tin‑plated copper wire and solder it to each electrode contact plate using lead‑free solder. Scratch the surface of each contact plate with a scalpel blade to improve wetting, then tin the plate with a small amount of solder before forming a solder ball to create a durable joint. Take extra care with palladium and gold contact plates, as their thin films can alloy with tin; avoid melting the film off the glass slide.

steps.title: Attach PTFE Tubing and Remove Isopropanol
steps.instruction: Cut PTFE microbore tubing (1/16 in OD – 1/32 in ID, Elveflow) to the required lengths with a scalpel. Lubricate the tubing insertion points with isopropanol to prevent PDMS cracking; no silicone sealant is needed because the PDMS seals with the slightly larger PTFE tubing. Bake the assembled cell at 60 °C–80 °C to evaporate residual isopropanol, then store the cell until use.

steps.title: Set Up Electrochemical Fluidic Connections
steps.instruction: Connect the primary inlet of the microfluidic cell to a syringe mounted in a programmable syringe pump or pressure pump. Connect the reference channel inlet to a free syringe; keep the side channel with the reference electrode stagnant during measurements, flushing it periodically with supporting electrolyte from its syringe. Place the entire cell inside an airtight polypropylene/silicone box (~10 × 15 cm², 1 mm thick) and purge with nitrogen (or argon) for at least 4 h, or overnight, to remove oxygen from the PDMS. The cell may also be stored in a glove box before use.

steps.title: Select Appropriate Syringes
steps.instruction: Use glass syringes with PTFE plungers (Gastight 1000 series LT, Hamilton) to minimize oxygen intrusion into the electrolyte. If disposable PP/PE syringes (Norm‑ject, Air‑Tite) are used, limit experiments to less than 1 h or when oxygen in the electrolyte is not critical.

steps.title: Connect Cell Inlets to Tubing
steps.instruction: Attach the cell inlets to the microfluidic cell using a PEEK luer adapter coupled to a PTFE ferrule and end connector (Elveflow) as shown in Fig. 9. Alternatively, a disposable stainless‑steel needle (Air‑Tite) with a slightly larger gauge than the tubing ID can be used, noting the increased dead volume and needle‑stick risk.

steps.title: Clean Microfluidic Cell After Use
steps.instruction: After each experiment (or after assembly), flush the cell with several milliliters of deionized water at a low flow rate overnight. Then purge the cell with air and bake at 65 °C–80 °C for a few hours or until dry. For thorough cleaning, flush sequentially with isopropanol or acetone, followed by isopropanol, bake again, and finally purge with water to remove any solvent residues.
